PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: character-david-freed-king-appearance
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Character guard: the row alone defines identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, hair, scars, costume, wounds, pose, and carried objects. Never turn a non-Jesus character into a Jesus lookalike.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
DAVID - FREED KING — APPEARANCE: FOUR-VIEW IDENTITY, ANATOMY, COSTUME, AND CONTINUITY REFERENCE.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

King David, the freed psalmist-king of Israel, captured at the exact liberation beat inside Hell's inner chamber after the chains of the righteous shatter. He is a Middle Eastern Semitic man of middle age, roughly late forties to mid-fifties in living appearance, height about five feet eight inches, athletic and compact with a noble upright posture that still reads as a shepherd-warrior who became a king. His frame is lean-muscular rather than bulky: broad enough shoulders for a former soldier, a still-strong neck and chest, hands that once held both sling and lyre now bearing the slight stiffness and dust of centuries of captivity. Skin is Mediterranean olive-tan, pale from the lightless prison yet still warm in undertone, with fine dust of ash and pale mineral grit lightly powdered across cheeks, brow, and the backs of the hands. A few healed nicks and age lines mark the face—crow's feet from squinting into sun and song, faint crease lines at the mouth from prayer and praise—but no gore, no modern scars, no tattoos.

Facial identity is locked across all views: a dignified, poetic face with a strong straight nose, high cheekbones softened by time, a firm but gentle jaw under a full long dark brown-to-near-black beard that shows silver threads at the chin and temples while remaining carefully shaped rather than matted wild. The beard falls to mid-chest length, dense and natural, with dry ash dust in the lower strands. Hair is long, dark brown-black, with complete crown coverage and full rear-head mass—thick waves that reach past the shoulders, parted naturally, with age-silvered strands at the temples and a few dry flyaways from the chamber air; the crown and back of the head are fully covered by hair with no balding patch, no second face, no rear features other than hair and neck. One human face exists only on the front of the head. Eyes are deep brown, large and reflective, with a distinctly musical and poetic quality—not warrior glare, not prophetic fire like Elijah, but recognition, hope, and the soft awe of a composer who finally hears the true Song. Brows are dark and expressive. Lips are slightly parted as if a psalm is about to rise. Expression across the set is spiritual recognition mixed with musical hope: the freed king who kept his harp even when its strings were broken.

Costume is faded royal Israelite court wear worn thin by ages in the abyss, never modern fashion. A long ankle-length outer robe in once-rich royal blue linen, now sunless-faded to dusty indigo and muted deep blue with worn patches at the hems and elbows; residual gold thread embroidery traces geometric and vine motifs along the neck opening, cuffs, and a vertical front panel, the metallic thread tarnished and broken in places so that gold catches light only as scattered flecks. Under the outer robe, a simpler earth-toned or off-white linen tunic shows at the neck and lower hem. A soft fabric sash or woven belt in faded gold-ochre and blue cinches the waist. Sandals are rough ancient leather, straps cracked and dusted. Fabric weave is visible: coarse linen hand-loom texture, frayed edges, ash-stained lower skirts as if he has knelt in the chamber dust. No crown is worn—he is the king freed, not enthroned—yet the cut and residual blue-gold palette still declare royalty. Continuity lock: same blue-gold faded garment set, same wear map, same dust pattern in every panel.

Carried prop continuity: David's ancient harp rests at his side or is held in one hand depending on view. The instrument is a small-to-medium ancient wooden frame harp or lyre-like biblical harp, dark aged wood with deep cracks, dry grain, and subtle old carvings suggesting praise motifs without any readable modern lettering. Strings are visibly broken—several gut or plant-fiber strings snapped and hanging limp, a few stubs remaining at the frame—symbolizing centuries of silenced music that will soon return. One hand may cradle the harp body against the hip or ribs; the free hand may open slightly toward an unseen source of warm divine light, fingers relaxed, clean anatomy, no extra digits.

Pose and multi-view lock for the four-view ingredients sheet: (1) frontal three-quarter portrait from mid-chest up, face clearly readable, eyes toward the light, harp neck or frame partially visible at the lower edge of frame; (2) full-body standing view, weight evenly on both feet with a slight step forward as if emerging from shadow into liberation, harp held at the left side, right hand softly raised or open toward divine radiance, robe hanging naturally with correct gravity folds; (3) true side profile, nose-to-beard silhouette clean, hair mass and beard depth accurate, harp silhouette clear; (4) rear-head and costume view showing complete dark hair covering the entire crown and back of the skull, neck, shoulder drape of the blue robe, gold-thread remnants along seams, no face on the back of the head. Body proportions, hand shape, garment construction, hairline, and harp design remain identical across every panel.

Environment context is Hell's inner chamber at the liberation beat: vast dark stone architecture receding softly out of focus behind him—high black pillars, residual blue torch light dying into warmer invading amber-gold as divine light begins to flood the prison. Broken chain links and pale dust may sit at the lower edge of the full-body panel as ground evidence of release, never dominating the character. Atmosphere is thin ash haze and faint volumetric god-rays cutting through cooler shadow, not pure black void and not full transformed white marble yet—this is the moment of emerging recognition between bondage and procession.

Lighting is cinematic and physically coherent for a photoreal live-action biblical epic: key light is warm ethereal amber-gold divine intrusion from above and slightly camera-right, approximately 5500–6500K god-ray quality that kisses forehead, cheekbones, beard edges, and the residual gold thread; fill is cool residual hell ambience from blue torches at roughly 2000K, soft and low, painting the shadow side of the robe with a cold indigo rim; a faint red underglow from distant hell stone may kiss the lower robe hem without turning the scene into pure crimson. Skin shows natural subsurface scatter in the warm key. Eyes catch a small specular of golden light. Color grade balances warm amber liberation against royal blue garment notes and cool shadow, deep but not crushed blacks, no neon, no modern grade LUTs look.

Camera language for the sheet: production reference multi-view layout, each panel like a high-end film character bible still, medium-format clarity, approximately 50–85mm portrait lens feel on faces and 35–50mm on full body, shallow depth of field isolating David from the chamber, aspect of each panel cinematic and clean. Photoreal human anatomy only—exact ears, clean five-fingered hands, correct clavicles and fabric weight. Texture priority: linen weave, tarnished gold thread, dry beard hair strands, wood grain and broken strings of the harp, dust on skin, soft volumetric light.

Tone is reverent biblical epic, not fantasy camp, not horror gore, not illustration or anime. No modern objects, no clocks, no firearms, no logos, no watermarks, no captions, no borders, no UI, no readable text or lettering anywhere on garments, harp, or background. One face only on the front of the head in every view. Lock identity: middle-aged King David, long dark aged-groomed hair and beard with silver threads, poetic brown eyes, faded royal blue and gold-thread robes, ancient broken-string harp, freed-soul dignity and musical hope inside Hell's chamber as divine light arrives.
